haiku-low.q1: It returns the popular-items list's first 20 IDs with fallback true and reason features_timeout or no_features. The model is not called.
haiku-low.q2: It keeps using stored feature values until they are over 6 hours old, then sends users to the popular-items fallback with reason features_stale.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow output has no route back to the API or any cache it reads. A shadow failure is logged and counted only; the user's response is unaffected.
haiku-low.q4: Users where hash(user_id, shadow_salt) mod 100 is below shadow_percent (10), while a shadow_version is set. Membership is fixed for each candidate's salt.
haiku-low.q5: The candidate needs a passing shadow evaluation (7 counted days, error under 0.5%, p99 under 80 ms), a passing feature availability check, and ML lead approval. The move to active is not yet enabled.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED. The document says product has not decided whether a live A/B stage exists, and the plan does not choose.
haiku-low.q7: Instances poll the serving config every 10 seconds and apply a changed revision. Inference instances preload, checksum and warm the new version, then atomically point at the new active_version.
haiku-low.q8: The shadow worker does its own online feature lookup for each required group, on a separate client, from the queue after the response is written. Nothing on the request path waits for it.
haiku-low.q9: A circuit breaker pauses shadow consumption when the API's feature p99 exceeds 20 ms or timeouts rise. Paused messages expire rather than drain late, and drops and skips are counted.
haiku-low.q10: Active responses go to the response log with model_version; shadow results go to the shadow log. A daily job joins them on request_id into per-version shadow metrics, including overlap@20 and rank correlation.
haiku-low.q11: The feature availability check (step 12) rejects setting a version as shadow, preload or active unless every required group is online, schema-matched and refreshed within 6 hours. Per-request checks also apply.
haiku-low.q12: One compare-and-set swaps active_version with previous_version and logs the change. The previous version is already warm on every instance, so it applies on the next poll, within about 10 seconds.

sonnet.q1: It returns the popular-items fallback (first 20 IDs of the in-memory popular list) with fallback: true and reason features_timeout (30 ms timeout, no retry), features_error or no_features. The model is not called.
sonnet.q2: The path keeps using stored feature records, since they are not purged and the TTL (e.g. 7 days) is well over 6 hours. It stops when a group's materialized_at is older than 6 hours: that group counts as missing, the user gets fallback with reason features_stale or features_incomplete, and the model is not called.
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow output has no route back to the API or to any cache the API reads, so it can never be shown to a user. Shadow failures cannot affect the response: the handoff happens after the response is written, uses a non-blocking bounded buffer with no awaits or retries, and drops the event (counted as shadow_dropped) if the buffer is full or the queue is unreachable.
sonnet.q4: Users where shadow_version is set and hash(user_id, shadow_salt) mod 100 < shadow_percent (10). The salt is fixed for one candidate's shadow run, so a given user is always in or always out. Only requests that reach step 5 and have in_shadow true are copied, after the response is written.
sonnet.q5: It needs the feature availability check (step 12): all required groups online, matching schema_version, last_success_at within 6 hours. It needs a shadow run passing the gate: at least 7 counted days, error rate under 0.5% and p99 inference under 80 ms, recorded as an evaluation record. It needs approval by an ML lead tied to that evaluation record. It needs the stage between approval and switch (A/B or direct) decided by product, because the tool stops at approved until then. It needs a preload (phase 1) with every inference instance reporting the version loaded and warmed up, within 15 minutes, before the flip.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. Product has not decided whether a live A/B test comes between shadow and the switch. The plan does not choose and is built so either option can be added. No A/B path is built now.
sonnet.q7: Each API and inference instance polls the serving config every 10 seconds. If revision changed, it applies the new snapshot. Inference instances load any version they lack, check its checksum and warm it up, then atomically point at the new active_version. The new version is preloaded before the flip, so no load happens on the request path and no redeploy is needed.
sonnet.q8: The shadow worker does its own online feature lookup for every group the candidate requires, on a separate rate-limited client, preferably against a read replica, and applies the same 6-hour freshness and completeness rule. It adds no user latency because the event goes to a bounded in-memory buffer after the response is written, then is published by a background thread to a separate queue. A separate pool of hosts consumes it, so nothing is awaited on the request path.
sonnet.q9: Backlog is dropped by expiry, not drained late: messages older than 5 minutes are skipped as skipped_stale_message, because late runs would see different features. Worker crashes are retried at most once. A circuit breaker pauses shadow consumption when the API's feature lookup p99 goes above 20 ms or its timeout rate rises, and paused messages expire. Shadow is the part that loses data. Drop and skip counts go into the metrics, and days with a drop rate over 5% are not counted.
sonnet.q10: Active responses go to the response log in the warehouse (step 7). Shadow outputs go to the shadow log (step 15). A daily job joins them on request_id and writes a shadow metrics table (one row per version per day). Gate metrics are error rate and p99 inference_ms. It also computes coverage and data-quality metrics, plus comparison-only metrics: overlap@20, rank correlation, catalog coverage, popular-item share and category spread.
sonnet.q11: The feature availability check (step 12) runs on any request to set shadow, preload or active version. Every required group must be online with a matching schema_version and last_success_at within 6 hours, otherwise the config change is rejected, naming the missing groups. It re-runs at gate evaluation and before the switch. The catalog blocks removing or changing the schema of a group needed by the active, previous or shadow version. At request time, steps 3 and 15 skip the model if features are missing or stale. A candidate needing new features must first have them added to materialization and have one successful run.
sonnet.q12: On-call runs rollback, or an automatic trigger from step 21 fires it. One compare-and-set swaps active_version with previous_version and writes the change history. The previous version is already loaded and warmed up on every instance, and instances poll every 10 seconds, so it takes effect within about 10 s plus a pointer swap. The tool waits until every instance reports the new revision and checks that the response-log model_version changed. It alerts on any instance still behind after 60 s, and non-converging instances are taken out of the load balancer. The guarantee covers only the previous version and depends on the config store being reachable.
